one_month_reasoning: The window runs to 2026-11-13. Scheduled events: the FOMC meeting on Oct 27-28 (src 28) and Q3 2026 results on Fri 2026-11-06 (src 14), where management said it would update 2026 and 2027 guidance (src 4). 2026 should land 'at or above the midpoint' of $6.8-7.6B (src 3/4); 2027 is trending to the low end of $7.4-7.8B before Cogentrix and Meta, plus ~$0.7B from those deals (src 4). A guide around $8.0-8.2B incl. deals is already expected, so roughly neutral. Today's -6.5% was the AI-power/IPP group selling off on the hot September CPI released at 08:30 ET (all items +0.6% m/m, +3.7% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +2.6% y/y; energy +5.2% m/m, src 22) with the 10-yr at 5.21% (src 21); CEG/TLN/NRG fell 5.5-6.2% and Vistra filed nothing (src 11, 18). Because the cause is a macro/rates factor that is still live into the FOMC, I assume only a small reversal: center ~$153.0 (+0.5%). Spread ~15% monthly vol (50%/3.5 = 14.3%, fattened for earnings and the FOMC), a 60/40 mix of 12% and 20% lognormals.

$700M = '~$0.7 billion of net present value of expected tax benefits' in Vistra's release (src 6) x 0.9 closing probability = $630M (~$1.9/share).

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount, not premium, and expected to persist through the horizon because its causes are structural and verified: 2028 is only ~72% hedged with ERCOT forwards 'meaningfully lower' and 2027 drifting to the low end (src 3, 4); PJM capacity revenue sits under a collar through 2029/30 and the 2030/31+ design is open, with a live consumer proposal to keep caps on existing generation (src 23, 24); the fleet is more gas-heavy than CEG's. Against NRG (8.9x), VST has the nuclear PTC floor and 20-year Meta contracts (src 7). Most of the all-peer set are regulated utilities that only bound the range.

thesis_break_reason: At $115 the pro forma equity (115 x ~340.6M shares incl. the 5.0M Cogentrix shares = $39.2B) plus pro forma net debt ($19.16B + $2.3B cash + $1.5B assumed debt = $22.96B) and $2.49B preferred/NCI is ~$64.6B, ~8.0x the ~$8.1B 2027 base. That is ~0.9x below NRG (8.9x), the cheapest IPP, and near my bear value ($110.6); ordinary 50%-vol noise rarely gets there without news. Round 1's $120 used horizon claims ($23.4B) instead of today's pro forma claims ($25.4B), which understated EV; on the pro forma basis $120 is 8.2x. Likely causes: PJM adopting a cap or administrative price for existing generation in 2030/31+ (the open flag), 2027 guidance on Nov 6 well below ~$8.1B, or an ERCOT forward collapse the 94%/72% 2027-28 hedges cannot absorb. Status of the flag (not tripped): the ~$325/~$175 collar covers RPM auctions only through the 2029/2030 delivery year (PJM answer, ER26-1556, src 23); PJM will evaluate investment incentives with stakeholders by end-2026 and then set the RPM path for 2030/31+ (src 23); the 2026-09-29 FERC order suspended the Reliability Backstop Procurement to 2027-02-28 and opened a section 206 proceeding (src 12). No filing to extend the cap past 2029/30 exists (EDGAR/PJM checked 2026-10-14), but at the 2026-07-15 PJM market-design workshop the Ohio Energy Group proposed a 'Legacy Auction' that would keep the cap and floor beyond 2029/2030 on existing generation (src 24): a live stakeholder proposal, not a PJM position.

reverse_dcf_check: At my 9.15% WACC and 2.0% terminal growth the DCF is $140.9 vs $171.0 for the 9.5x leg; the engine says the multiple implies a WACC of ~8.3% at 2.0% growth. In Gordon terms, 9.5x NTM EBITDA with ~58% EBITDA-to-FCFF conversion (20% tax on EBIT, capex ~10% of revenue) at 9.15% implies perpetual FCFF growth of ~2.9%: 9.5 = 0.58 x (1+g) / (0.0915 - g). That is above the 2.0-2.5% I find plausible once a possible 2030/31+ PJM cap on existing units (p 0.4, -$3.4/share), ERCOT oversupply (-$3.5) and the AI-capex low case (-$7.5) are priced. So I do not raise the multiple to the 10.6x peer median; I keep 9.5x (about where VST trades today, the market's implied discount rate) and let the 30% DCF weight pull the blend toward the cash-flow value. The round-1 9.0x exit is equivalent to ~2.35% growth at 9.15% ($153 DCF); the Gordon 2.0% form is used instead.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 SBC $113M (F43; TTM $134M, F46). Peers' NTM multiples are on consensus adjusted EBITDA that excludes stock comp (Talen Q2 release, src 27; peers.md, src 20), so VST's EBITDA and FCFF are pre-SBC (engine ebit_basis 'adjusted', sbc_treatment 'dilution') and SBC enters once, as ~1.1M extra shares by the horizon (134 / ~$150 x 1.25 years) inside the 334.3M count. Round 1 deducted SBC from FCFF and also added the shares, counting it twice; the P/E leg (EPS after SBC) was dropped. Post-horizon dilution of ~0.3%/yr is not in the DCF (~-$0.4/share).

reasoning: Round 2. Cause of the drop, now pinned: September CPI was released 2026-10-14 08:30 ET at +0.6% m/m and +3.7% y/y (core +0.3% m/m, +2.6% y/y; energy +5.2% m/m) (BLS, src 22), with the 10-yr at 5.21% (src 21). VST closed -6.5% with CEG -5.5%, TLN -6.2% and NRG -5.9%, against SPY -1.1% and XLU -0.3% (src 18). Vistra filed nothing (latest 8-K 2026-10-05, src 11). The move is sector-wide, a rates/AI-power factor sell-off, not company news, so fair value does not move because of it. Changes from round 1 (supervisor feedback, verified at the primaries): (1) SBC is now counted once, as dilution, on pre-SBC EBITDA like the peers; round 1 deducted it in FCFF and also added the shares. (2) WACC is 8.5% -> 9.15%, on rf 5.21% and a 6.5% marginal debt cost (new 7.0-7.25% junior notes). (3) The DCF terminal is now Gordon 2.0% instead of a 9.0x exit, which was equivalent to ~2.35% growth and reused peer multiples: DCF $155 -> $141. (4) The P/E leg is dropped. (5) The Cogentrix tax NPV now cites Vistra's own release (src 6), not The Fly. (6) The AI-capex low case (src 26) is added to the bear case and long-dated risks. New in-lane evidence: the 424B5 shows the junior notes may fund redemption of the 8.0%/7.0% preferred (claims-neutral, src 25); a 2026-07-15 PJM workshop presentation by the Ohio Energy Group proposes keeping the cap and floor on existing generation beyond 2029/30 (src 24). PJM's own answer leaves the 2030/31+ path to after its end-2026 stakeholder review (src 23), so I raise the PJM-cap probability from 0.35 to 0.4. Valuation: 9.5x NTM adjusted EBITDA of $8.41B = $171.0 (70%), DCF $140.9 (30%), fair value $162.0 (round 1 $165.0). Scenarios $110.6 / $162.0 / $212.4 at 25/50/25, lognormal mix with 30% within-scenario vol (~39% total), so the 12-month median is ~$158.7, ~4% above spot. Thesis break moves from $120 to $115, ~8.0x pro forma 2027 EBITDA. The sell-side median target of $210 (src 19) is near my bull case and was not used. About 8 follow-up searches/fetches; www.sec.gov pages were read via WebFetch, data.sec.gov JSON directly.

19,160 + Cogentrix cash 2,300 and assumed debt 1,500 (src 5) - ~15 months of Adj. FCFbG at ~4,300/yr = ~5,400 (2026 guidance midpoint, src 3) + growth spend ex-Cogentrix ~1,500 (part of the $4.5-5B 2026-27 growth allocation, src 4) + buybacks ~1,250 (remaining ~$1.2B authorization by YE2027, src 3) + common and preferred dividends ~580 = ~20,900. inputs_detail.input: NTM adjusted EBITDA at horizon (Q4-2027 to Q3-2028)
inputs_detail.derivation: Model rows: FY2027 8,104 (= low end of the $7.4-7.8B 2027 midpoint opportunity, which management said is trending to the lower end, src 4, plus ~$700M from Cogentrix (~$4.0B / 7.25x = ~$550M, Vistra release src 6) and the Meta PPA premium (src 4, 7)); FY2028 8,497 (+~5%: full Meta operating delivery by YE2027 (src 7), PJM capacity flat at $325 vs $333 (src 8), ERCOT soft, only ~72% hedged (src 3)). NTM = 0.21 x FY2027 + 0.79 x FY2028. Pre-SBC, the same basis as peer consensus adjusted EBITDA (src 27). The thin FMP consensus for the window (~$9,370M, 1-4 analysts, src 19) is not used; this sits ~10% below it.

Peer NTM EV/EBITDA median 10.6x, range 8.9x (NRG) to 11.8x (CEG), on consensus adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA (src 20, 27). VST trades ~9.5-9.8x today: EV ~$72.7B (152.2 x 335.6M = $51.1B + $19.16B net debt + $2.49B preferred/NCI) on ~$7.4-7.6B NTM EBITDA before the deals. 9.5x is about where it trades now, ~1.1x below the median, between NRG and TLN. The discount reflects merchant ERCOT exposure (2028 only ~72% hedged, src 3), the undecided PJM 2030/31+ design with a consumer push to cap existing generation (src 23, 24), and the gas-heavy fleet vs CEG. No premium is claimed.
FY2025 revenue 17,586 (F3); TTM to 2026-06-30 18,985 (F6) supports ~19,600 for FY2026; FY2027 adds Cogentrix's 5,500 MW (src 5,6) and Meta deliveries; later years grow with load at 3-4%.
Capex FY2025 2,752 (F57), TTM 2,866 (F60, ~15% of TTM revenue, includes growth projects); declines as the Permian peakers and other growth projects are completed.

FY2025 SBC 113 / revenue 17,586 = 0.64% (F43, F3); TTM 134 (F46) on ~19,600 FY2026 revenue = ~0.7%. Under sbc_treatment 'dilution' it is carried as ~1.1M extra shares by the horizon instead of a cash cost.

Cost of equity 10.71% = 10-yr UST 5.21% on 2026-10-13 (src 21) + beta ~1.1 (judgment for a merchant IPP) x 5% ERP. Pre-tax marginal debt cost 6.5%: TTM average 5.8% (interest 1,132 / debt 19,595, F81/F98) is below today's marginal cost, shown by the 7.000%/7.250% junior notes issued 2026-09-24 (src 9); x (1 - 20%) = 5.2%. Preferred ~7.5% (8.0%/7.0% series, src 25). Weights on EV $72.7B: 70.3% equity, 26.4% net debt, 3.4% preferred -> 9.16%, used as 9.15% (round 1: 8.5% with 5.24% rf and 5.8% debt cost).

inputs_detail.input: Terminal value: Gordon growth after FY2029
